SHIRTSCANNER
Home Providers

narrative.overview: ShirtScanner is a tool first and a poster second: one query, streamed across a wall of Chinese marketplace stores, results arriving like a live score feed. Color follows the retro kit: clean cool white pitch surface, royal blue action, red accent, and a single crest-gold detail. Typography is one voice (Inter), pressed hard into weight and case contrast. The phone is the primary canvas: single column, thumb reach, 44px touch targets, no hover-only affordances.
keyCharacteristics: Cool white body, blue-undertow ink, two-block kit palette (royal blue + red)
One typeface, uppercase extra-bold display, no second family
Flat surfaces: hairline borders and tonal layering, not shadows
Sharp, slightly-curved controls (6-12px), full-pill only for chips and progress
Dense, results-first layout; no decorative sections
Pocket-first: single column, thumb-reachable actions, 44px touch targets, no hover-only controls

rules.name: The Pitch-White Rule
rules.body: The body is always cool white with a trace of the blue hue. No cream, sand, beige, parchment, or warm-tinted surfaces anywhere. Warmth is a kit color, not a paper color.

rules.name: The Two-Block Rule
rules.body: Kit Blue and Kit Red appear as solid blocks next to each other, like a jersey. Never as a gradient between them, never as stripes, never blended.

rules.name: The Crest-Gold Rule
rules.body: Crest Gold is a two-touch maximum per screen. Condensed on price and standout moments only.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only family. No second display font, no mono unless a future feature produces literal code or query text.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Uppercase display never goes tighter than -0.03em letter-spacing. -0.05em and tighter looks cramped, not bold.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Only-Display Rule
rules.body: All-caps is reserved for display headings and the wordmark. Body copy, labels, and buttons never sit in all caps.

rules.name: The Flat Pitch Rule
rules.body: Depth is conveyed by hairline borders and tonal layering, never by shadows. Shadows are reserved for floating overlays only, and no shadow blur exceeds 8px.

rules.name: The Pocket-First Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a phone screen may depend on hover, on a tablet-width layout, or on a tap target under 44px. Every action a user takes while standing with one hand must be reachable in the bottom half of the screen. When a desktop pattern cannot collapse cleanly to a phone, it is replaced, not squeezed.

dos: Do keep the body Pitch White, cool, with the blue undertow. Warmth comes from Kit Red and the type, never from the page.
Do use Kit Blue for every primary action and Kit Red for counts, down-status, and destructive actions, as solid blocks.
Do cap display sizes at clamp(..., 4.5rem) and display tracking at -0.03em.
Do honor WCAG 2.1 AA: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text, visible focus rings, and prefers-reduced-motion alternates for every animation.
Do surface honest signals: what was found, what was missed, which providers are up, and the direct link to check the store yourself.
Do give every animation a reduced-motion fallback (crossfade or instant), and ease out with exponential curves when motion runs.
Do design on a phone first: single column, 44px minimum touch targets, primary action in thumb reach, no hover-only interactions.
Do reset the first render against the largest and smallest expected screens and the longest heading words; if a heading overflows, reduce the clamp or rewrite the copy.
donts: Don't ship any interaction that only exists on hover, or any tap target under 44px on its smallest dimension.
Don't squeeze a desktop pattern onto a phone; collapse tables to stacked rows and grids to single column, or replace the pattern.
Don't use gradients, gradient text, or background-clip text. Color is solid blocks, per the Two-Block Rule.
Don't use glassmorphism, blur-glass cards, or 32px+ radii on cards or sections.
Don't build hero-metric templates (big number, label, supporting stats) or identical repeated card grids.
Don't ship fake urgency: no countdown timers, no 'only 3 left' pricing, no hype pricing, no spin-to-win.
Don't use side-stripe borders > 1px as colored accents on cards or alerts.
Don't pair a 1px border with a wide (>=16px) drop shadow on the same element.
Don't use clipart-style, hand-drawn sketchy SVG illustrations, grunge filters, or repeating-diagonal stripe backgrounds.
Don't put a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section. The Kit-Number chip is the only sanctioned numbered motif.
Don't use the streamline/empower/seamless/supercharge family of marketing words.
Don't render body copy or buttons in all caps, and don't set display tracking tighter than -0.03em.
